title_kr: Finding Kindfulness:  How Prosocial Practices Boost Health and Well-being

authors.name: 에밀리아나 사이먼 토마스
authors.affiliation: Greater Good Science Center, UC Berkeley

abstract_kr: Discovering strategies to uphold, sustain, and even improve human health and well-being has been a core goal for centuries. Many thinkers and disciplines have published ideas, practices, exercises, and activities for this purpose, including philosophical and belief systems, cultural values and ideals, and specific behaviors. Modern scientific inquiry into well-being, beyond the absence of mental or physical health challenges or clinical conditions, became established in the late 1900s, and has grown exponentially into a global literature. This article proposes that kindfulness, which includes behaviors and characteristics that can be described as both mindful and kind, enhances prosociality, which boosts lifelong health and well-being. Prosociality is an innate human drive that compels people to do things that benefit others or society as a whole, like help, share, cooperate, and console. Preliminary and published findings from projects designed to offer practical and secular resources for strengthening kindfulness through freely accessible internet-based programs offer preliminary support for this claim. Showcasing the meaning of kindfulness, its links to prosociality, beneficial impact on health and well-being, and a variety of potentially effective strategies for promoting it, this work offers a contemporary, applied perspective on the promise of kindfulness.

title_kr: 허응당 보우(虛應堂 普雨)의 ‘일정(一正)’과 주자(朱熹) 이기심성론(理氣⼼性論) 구조의 비교 - 본체 ․ 심성 ․ 수양의 회통을 중심으로 -
title_en: The Harmonization of Essence, Mind, and Cultivation in Heo Eung-dang Bowu and Zhu Xi: A Comparative Inquiry into Iljeong (一正) and the Li–Qi–Mind–Nature Theory (理氣心性論)
abstract_kr: Weon heesoo·Ven JeongDo(Seowangmo) This study compares Heo Eung-dang Bowu’s (Hŭŭngdang Powu, 1510–1565) theory of Iljeong (一正) with Zhu Xi’s (1130–1200) theory of Li–Qi–Mind–Nature (理氣心性論), in order to explore the possibility of convergence between Buddhist and Confucian perspectives on the philosophy of mind and nature. Bowu regarded Il (一, the One) as the ontological essence (Che, 體) and Jeong (正, the Right) as its moral manifestation (Yong, 用), interpreting the mind (Sim, 心) as both the source of the cosmos and the field of moral realization. In contrast, Zhu Xi emphasized the harmony of the Moral Mind (Dao sim, 道心) and the Human Mind (In sim, 人心) within the dual structure of Li (principle) and Qi (vital force). Analyzing their systems through the triadic correspondence of Il–Li (本體), Jeong–Sim (心性), and Pyŏngsang sim–Gyŏ gyeong (修養), this study reveals that Bowu’s non-dual (bul i, 不二) approach transforms Zhu Xi’s ethical metaphysics into an experiential ontology of moral practice. The findings demonstrate that Bowu’s Iljeong philosophy unifies being and practice, enlightenment and conduct, offering a paradigm of moral realization that bridges Buddhist intuition and Confucian rationality within East Asian thought.

title_kr: 懶翁惠勤의 수륙재 小參에 대한  정신분석학적 고찰
title_en: A Psychoanalytic Study of the small sermons in the Naong Hwasang Yurok (『懶翁和尙語錄』)
abstract_kr: This study explores the small sermons (⼩參) in the Naong Hwasang Yurok (『懶翁和尙語錄』) through a psychoanalytic lens, focusing on Naong Hye-geun (懶翁惠勤)'s public teachings during Suryukjae ceremonies. The small sermons reveal Master Naong's efforts to stabilize people's livelihoods and care for their inner peace, as seen in his performance of the National Suryukjae Ceremony upon the passing of Princess NokukDaejang and King Gongmin.To explore the intersubjective exchange between Naong and the masses, this study first analyzes the psychoanalytic psychological mechanisms found in the Story of Muian Rescues His Mother featuring Sutra on the Ullambana Festival. On this basis, it identifies patterns of projective identification, mourning, and sublimation as defense mechanisms at work in the small sermons.Furthermore, Naong's vow to renounce the world for liberation from birth and death, together with his final Nirvana Buddhist rite, culminates in a view in which life and death are one and the same, and the ordinary mind is the Way. Through these Zen principles embodied in the Suryukjae Ceremony, Naong guides not only the deceased but also the assembly to take refuge in the Three Jewels.This act of taking refuge can be understood as a psychological mechanism that opens new horizons for contemporary psychological approaches to death.

title_kr: 백파긍선의 선사상에 비추어 본 『단경』의 36대법 고찰
title_en: A Study on the Thirty-six Pairs of Opposites in the Platform Sutra in Light of Baekpa Geungseon's Seon Thought
abstract_kr: Huineng's teaching of the "thirty-six pairs of opposites" is a doctrinal system designed to guide practitioners to detach from the extremes of existence and non-existence and to embody the wisdom of the Middle Way based on Self-nature. Baekpa Geungseon reinterpreted this doctrine through his unique theoretical framework, which includes the "Three Statements," "Qi-yong (Capacity and Function)," and "True Emptiness and Marvelous Existence." This study analyzed how Baekpa structurally integrated Huineng's teachings into his own Seon thought. The analysis revealed that Baekpa correlated the operational method of the thirty-six pairs—specifically the "blocking of both extremes" and their "appearance and disappearance"—with the expedient means of the "New Perfumed Three Statements" (also referred to as Marvelous Existence or Qi-yong). Furthermore, he connected the realization of "Self-nature," the ultimate source of these pairs, directly to the enlightened state of the "Original One Statement" (or True Emptiness).Through this reinterpretation, Baekpa defined the theory of the thirty-six pairs not merely as a list of opposites, but as the "First Statement Patriarchal Seon," which integrates expedient means with ultimate truth. By organically linking these two previously distinct concepts, this research verified the internal consistency of Baekpa's Seon thought and illuminated the creative process of its inheritance and deepening.

title_kr: 서울국제명상엑스포의 여정과 비전
title_en: The journey and vision of the Seoul International Meditation Expo
abstract_kr: Buddhism has developed diverse practice traditions throughout its long history, reflecting the changing times and regions. Among them, Seon Buddhism (Seon) has established itself as a practice tradition that seeks enlightenment through intuitive insight into the nature of the mind. Originating in China, Seon evolved into a practice-centered Buddhism through the ideological transmission from Bodhidharma to the Sixth Patriarch Huineng. It has since had a profound influence across East Asia, including Korea and Japan. This Seon philosophy emphasizes the principles of “directly pointing to the human mind” (jikji insim) and “seeing one's nature and becoming Buddha” (gyeonseongseongbul) over doctrinal discussions, emphasizing inner awareness and freedom. In modern times, the essence of Seon philosophy is being reinterpreted with new meanings, combining it with various forms of meditation. Modern practices such as mindfulness, convergence meditation, digital meditation, and AI meditation are bringing the traditional Seon philosophy of “Ipsahaeng” (translation of “introduction to the mind”) and “Sammu-sasang” (traditional non-traditional thinking) into the lives of modern people.This encounter is significant not only because it changes the form of practice, but also because it explores the contemporary challenges of restoring human mental health and social relationships through practice.The Seoul International Meditation Expo is a representative venue where these traditional Seon ideas and various streams of modern meditation converge, striving to globalize meditation grounded in Buddhist spirit. By establishing a convergence between Eastern and Western meditation traditions, scientific mind research, and social practice, the Expo aims to suggest a new direction for human spiritual culture.With this in mind, we will explore the ideology behind the journey and vision of the sixth Seoul International Meditation Expo. This will provide an opportunity to explore how the profound traditions of Seon Buddhism live and breathe in our educational settings and society today.

title_kr: 본래성불의 치유적 함의와 현대적 적용
title_en: Therapeutic Implications of Innate Buddhahood and Its Contemporary Applications
abstract_kr: This study aims to reinterpret the Seon Buddhist concept of innate Buddhahood (Bonrae seongbul) through a contemporary psychological lens, proposing it as a fundamental healing resource inherently present in human beings. Drawing on a literature-based inquiry and theoretical analysis, the study argues that the primary impetus for healing lies not in external intervention or deficit compensation, but in the recovery and awakening of one's essential nature. Focusing on balsim (the arousal of the aspiration for enlightenment; bodhicitta) and hoegwang banjo (turning the light inward) as practical pathways, it further suggests that awakening to innate Buddhahood functions as an archetypal structure of self-affirmation and is structurally homologous to psychological mechanisms underlying resilience and self-actualization. Moving beyond symptom-reduction-oriented technical approaches, the study proposes an ontological, solutionoriented healing framework that elucidates the innate capacity for spontaneous healing.

title_kr: 보조지눌의 선병(禪病) 이해와 대치법 연구- 명상 지도의 관점에서 -
title_en: Zen Sickness (禪病) in Bojo Jinul's Philosophy: Countermeasures and Meditation Guidance Applications
abstract_kr: This study examines the concept and classification of seonbyeong (禪病, meditation sickness) in Bojo Jinul's (普照知訥, 1158-1210) Beopjip Byeolhaengnok Jeolyo Byeongip Sagi (法集別⾏錄節要幷⼊私記), and explores corresponding countermeasures. Through a full textual review and philological analysis, thirteen types of meditation sickness were identified and systematised into five categories: hindrance of views, disharmony, psychological obstacles, laziness, and arrogance. The countermeasures were organised as follows: unity of meditation and doctrine, cultivation of concentration and wisdom, practice of compassion and merit, observance of precepts, and reliance on the teacher's guidance. The significance of this study lies in providing a theoretical framework that connects Jinul's traditional discourse on meditation sickness with contemporary research on meditation-related side effects (MRSE), thereby offering resources for risk management and counselling in modern meditation practice.

title_kr: 간화선 집중수행의 심리생리적 효과 : 뇌파지수와 마음챙김 주의 자각(K-MAAS) 척도 기반
title_en: Psychophysiological Effects of Ganhwa Seon Intensive Practice: Based on EEG Indices and the Korean Mindful Attention Awareness Scale (K-MAAS)
abstract_kr: This study examined the effects of a short-term intensive Ganhwa Seon meditation retreat on practitioners' psychophysiological indicators, focusing on mindfulness levels and EEG-based neurophysiological measures. Participants engaged in a 5-night, 6-day Ganhwa Seon intensive retreat, and data were collected using a pre-post comparison design. Psychological indicators were assessed using the Korean version of the Mindful Attention Awareness Scale (K-MAAS), while physiological indicators were evaluated with NeuroHarmony-based EEG measurements, including attention, activation, emotional index, anti-stress index, and overall brain index.The results indicated that even short-term intensive practice led to a significant increase in mindfulness. EEG measures also showed positive changes, such as increased basic rhythms and activation in the left hemisphere, as well as improvements in attention, emotional index, and anti-stress index. These findings suggest that Ganhwa Seon practice effectively enhances awareness of the present moment, alleviates emotional tension and stress responses, and promotes neural stability. However, no statistically significant changes were observed in right hemisphere activation or self-regulation indices, raising the possibility that the effects of the practice may be localized to specific brain regions.This study suggests the potential for Ganhwa Seon to be extended beyond its traditional religious framework as a contemplative tool for enhancing psychological awareness and emotional regulation in modern contexts.

title_kr: 자기 초월적인 ‘무아’에서 관계지향적 ‘대비’로 전환되는 현대적 불교 인성론 연구
title_en: A Study on the Transition from Anātman (Self-Transcendence) to Mahākaruṇā (Relational Compassion) : Toward an Integrative Buddhist Personality Theory
abstract_kr: This study explores the development of Buddhist personality theory through the transition from anātman (non-self) in early Buddhism to mahākaruṇā (great compassion) in Mahāyāna Buddhism. The early doctrine of non-self, analyzed through the five aggregates (pancaskandha), dismantles the illusion of a permanent self and provides the foundation for the arahant, an ideal of self-transcendence that achieves liberation by eradicating attachment and delusion. Mahāyāna Buddhism, however, places great compassion at the center, presenting the bodhisattva who vows to remain in the world until all beings are liberated. This compassion arises not merely from sentiment but from the realization of emptiness (śūnyatā) and dependent origination (pratītya-samutpāda), which reveal the inseparability of self and others.The study argues that non-self and compassion are integrated in the principle of “seeking enlightenment above and delivering beings below” (śaṅkubodhi-hāhuà-zhòngshēng), where wisdom and compassion function as inseparable dimensions of an ideal personality. This integration, exemplified in the Buddha and great bodhisattvas, also resonates with modern psychology, particularly Kohlberg's postconventional morality and Maslow's self-transcendence. In response to the challenges of modern individualism and the erosion of empathy, Buddhist personality theory offers a practical vision for cultivating wisdom and compassion as the foundation for solidarity and genuine human flourishing.

title_kr: 무호 백성욱의 불교사상과 수행법
title_en: Muho Baek Seong-uk's Buddhist Thought and Practice
abstract_kr: This paper examines the life and thought of Muho Baek Seong-uk (無號 白性郁), alongside two prominent figures who laid the foundations of Dongguk University's Buddhist tradition—Seokjeon Park Han-young and Manhae Han Yong-un—in celebration of Dongguk university's 120th anniversary. In line with this theme, the paper critically reviews Baek Seong-uk's life and philosophy. It also introduces recent research on Baek Seong-uk, especially after the establishment of the Baek Seong-uk Research Institute in 2018, and argues that some previous studies have mythologized his figure.Through this exploration, the paper reveals Baek Seong-uk's contributions to Dongguk University’s Buddhist tradition and clarifies the characteristics of his Buddhist philosophy and practice.This study investigates the life, Buddhist philosophy, and meditation practices of Muho Baek Seong-uk (1897-1981), who was the first Korean Buddhist scholar to study in Germany during the Japanese colonial period and obtain a doctoral degree. Along with Kim Beop-rin, who studied in France, Baek Seong-uk was a key figure in introducing Western Buddhist studies to Korea.He was not only an independence activist and Buddhist scholar but also a politician and educational administrator, leading a multifaceted life outside the typical monastic or lay roles.Baek Seong-uk asserted that by repeatedly reading and meditating on the Diamond Sutra (⾦剛經), one could acquire the powers of sukmyeongtong (knowledge of fate), tashim-tong (knowledge of others' minds), and nujin-tong (attainment of all-encompassing knowledge). His Buddhist philosophy and meditation methods can be understood in this context. The paper also raises the question of how Baek Seong-uk's thought and practice should be positioned within the tradition of Dongguk Buddhism.

title_kr: 화두참구에 기반한 현대인의 실존적 문제 해결 방안 모색-『서장(書狀)』과『몽산법어(蒙山法語)』를 중심으로 -
title_en: Exploring Solutions to Modern Existential Problems Based on Hwadu investigation: Focusing on Seojang by Dahui Zongao and Beopeo by Mongsan
abstract_kr: The rapid advancement of technology and the expansion of materialism in contemporary society have created a new cultural environment in which reality and virtuality are interwoven, fundamentally transforming the nature of human life. Amidst these changes, modern individuals face a wide range of existential suffering, including identity confusion, isolation, emptiness, anxiety, and depression. This study examines such existential issues from the perspective of contemplative practice and explores the modern applicability of hwadu investigation as a potential solution. The study compares and analyzes the Hwadu practice systems found in Dahui Zongao's Seojang and Mongsan Deokyi's Beopgeo, and discusses how Ganhwa Seon can be expanded as a practical approach applicable to modern life.This research presents the contemporary application of hwadu investigation in three main aspects. First, it offers a transformative process of self-discovery for individuals who have lost their sense of identity due to digital addiction and confusion. Second, it addresses the root causes of relational conflict and isolation, and suggests the possibility of healing through the realization of interrelated existence.Third, through the dialogical guidance and verification process with a teacher, practitioners are encouraged to explore the fundamental nature of life while gaining therapeutic insight into emotional difficulties. In particular, the practice of posing essential questions based on hwadu and engaging in reflective inquiry serves as a form of daily contemplative practice. With proper guidance, practitioners can maintain accuracy and direction in their spiritual path.In conclusion, this study demonstrates that hwadu investigation in Ganhwa Seon can serve as a direct and practical method for addressing the existential problems of modern individuals.Furthermore, it suggests that Korean Ganhwa Seon, rather than remaining a traditional monastic practice, holds the potential to be established as a universal value capable of contributing to the global discourse on mental and spiritual well-being.

title_kr: 만해 한용운의 간화선과 구세에 대한 고찰
title_en: A Study on Manhae Han Yong-un's Ganhwaseon and Salvation of the World
abstract_kr: This study examined Manhae's aspect as a Master of Ganhwaseon and his View of Salvation of the World. This discussion was conducted from three major perspectives. First, Manhae's View of the Ganhwaseon was discussed. Manhae obtained enlightenment by practicing the Hwadu from the perspective of Linji School and interpreted Seon with it. Manhae insisted on Seon that is not bound by Seon by integrating it into our specific lives and daily lives, and emphasized Practice of Hwadu as a prerequisite for approaching this enlightenment of Seon. Second, Manhae's view of salvation of the world is revealed in his enlightenment poetry, but also in <The Revitalizing Reformation of Chosun Buddhism>, which he completed before attaining enlightenment. Manhae emphasized that the purpose of Practice of Seon is salvation of the world. Third, I examined the perspective of salvation advocated by Manhae through his ‘Seon outside Seon’, ‘public reformation in different species’ of <Annotation to The Ten Profound Verses>, and ‘the construction of popular Buddhism.’ This view of salvation advocated by Manhae was further concretized through the ‘construction of popular Buddhism,’ which did not divide one's own liberation and the salvation of other beings into two.

title_kr: AI기반 ‘마인드 업로딩’에 관한 불교적 관점 - 자아 동일성 논쟁을 중심으로 -
title_en: Buddhist Perspectives on AI-based Mind Uploading : Centering on the Debate over Personal Identity
abstract_kr: This study critically examines AI-based mind uploading, which is becoming feasible through advancements in deep learning, from the perspective of Buddhist anātman (non-self) doctrine. The rapid development of brain-computer interface (BCI) technologies, exemplified by Neuralink, along with the anticipated technological singularity around 2045, has brought the digitalization of human consciousness into the realm of realistic discourse. Mind uploading, pursued through whole brain emulation, gradual replacement, or conscious uploading methods, embodies a transhumanist aspiration toward digital immortality by transferring human consciousness onto a digital substrate. Nevertheless, significant debate persists regarding criteria for self-identity in this process. In addressing this issue, Buddhist anātman doctrine rejects the existence of any permanent, independent self, instead conceptualizing the individual as an interdependent aggregation of the five skandhas. In early Buddhism, personal continuity is explained via the causal flow of karma and consciousness, offering an important insight for the mind-uploading debate on personal identity. Existing theories―biological identity, functionalism, computationalism, psychological continuity, and pattern identity―all assume some form of substantial self and thus reveal fundamental limitations when assessed from the perspective of non-self. As an alternative, this study proposes the ‘karmaconsciousness identity theory’, contending that only when a replicated entity inherits both the karmic momentum and the causal continuity of consciousness from the original can it be considered to possess the same identity in a Buddhist sense. Ultimately, mind uploading constitutes merely another form of ‘simulated rebirth’ so long as ignorance and craving remain unextinguished, thus underscoring that true liberation lies not in technological immortality but in freedom from attachment.

title_kr: 대주혜해(大珠慧海)의 『돈오입도요문론』과  『제방문인참문어록』 성립 고찰
title_en: A Study of the Establishment of Donoipdoyomun (『頓悟⼊道要門論』) and Jebangmuninchammuneorok (『諸⽅門人參問語錄』) by Daejuhyehae
abstract_kr: This paper considered the establishment of Donoipdoyomun (『頓悟 入道要門論』), known as a thesis written by Daejuhyehae himself, and Jebangmuninchammuneorok (『諸⽅門人參問語錄』) which was recorded by a third party.Although the year of birth of Daeju is unknown and a brief biography is also presented, many records show that he is a disciple of Majo.However, in the Donoipdoyomun (『頓悟入道要門論』) a number of Shinhoe-eorok (神會語錄) are cited instead of Majo-eok. For that reason, first, the formation of the Majo-eok was late, so the Daeju would not have been able to refer to it. Second, it is assumed that the Daeju recognized Hyeneung (慧能), Majo (⾺祖), and Shinhoe (神會) as the same kind of thinkers who shared the essentials of Southern Zen Buddhism (南宗禪), so he had no qualms about quoting the Shinhoe-eorok (神會語錄).The Donoipdoyomun (『頓悟入道要門論』) has the form of an early Zen composition characterized by question-and-answer and citation of scriptures, and cites records that cannot be seen except for copies of Tunhuang (敦煌), including the Shinhoe-eorok (神會語錄). Based on the record that Majo authorized the book and the ‘建安魏信刊’ in the preface of the Geumtaek (⾦澤) manuscript of Donoipdoyomun (『頓悟 入道要門論』) it seems to have been established and distributed during the Tang (唐) Dynasty.Since Jebangmuninchammuneorok (『諸⽅門人參問語錄』) is partially cited in Jodangjip (『祖堂集』) and Jonggyeongnok (『宗鏡錄』) and Jonggyeongnok (『宗鏡錄』) contains many contents that are not included in Jebangmuninchammuneorok (『諸⽅門人參問語錄』), it is presumed that the original Jebangmuninchammuneorok (『諸⽅門人參 問語錄』) and alternative version existed, and it is certain that it was distributed during the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms (五代十國). It seems that it has its current form before and after the publication of Transmission of the Lamp (『景德傳燈錄』). It was distributed by Myohyeop (妙叶) during the Ming (明) Dynasty that Donoipdoyomun (『頓悟入道要門論』) and Jebangmuninchammuneorok (『諸⽅門人參問語 錄』) were combined.The two books contain various citations of the scriptures and early Zen book, and discussions with various disputant, indicating the trends of the Buddhist community at the time, and assessing the ideological impact on the Daeju.

title_kr: 불교기반 명상 프로그램[8-행복한 바른 명상: 행복한 봄]에 대한 연구 - 프로그램 핵심 전략과 개요 중심으로 -
title_en: A Study on Buddhist-Based Meditation Program [8-Happy & Right Meditation: View]
abstract_kr: The ‘8-Happy & Right Meditation’ program is an 8-session Buddhist-based meditation initiative grounded in the Noble Eightfold Path and Threefold Training (ethics, concentration, wisdom). It promotes psychological well-being while pursuing the Buddhist objectives of alleviating suffering and attaining ultimate happiness. Addressing the side effects (e.g., anxiety, delusion) of conventional psycho-therapeutic meditation approaches detached from Buddhist roots, this program integrates ethical practice, systematic cultivation, and accessibility, utilizing Korean Seon Buddhism's Ganhwaseon for profound insight and practical application.It has the Key Features compared to other meditation programs as the below. 1. Systematic Practice Rooted in Buddhist Orthodoxy: It harmonizes ethics, concentration, and wisdom through the Noble Eightfold Path and Threefold Training, employing Ganhwaseon to experientially explore suffering's cessation and happiness. 2. Phased Approach and Accessibility: Structured in three phases ‘Happy View’, ‘Happy Insight’, and ‘Happy Awakening’ it facilitates a gradual progression from knowledge to wisdom for participants with meditation experience, ensuring accessibility for beginners. 3.Balance of Experiential Insight and Self-Reflection: Through insight, loving-kindness, and Ganhwaseon meditations, it enables direct experience of the Three Marks of Existence and dependent origination, fostering deep insight and long-term emotional stability.Reinterpreting Buddhist teachings for contemporary contexts, this program minimizes meditation's adverse effects and offers an alternative approach that meets modern psychological and spiritual needs through ethical practice and experiential insight.

title_kr: 석전 박한영의 교육 철학과 불교 인재 양성
title_en: Seokjeon Park Han-young's Educational Philosophy and the Cultivation of Buddhist Talent
abstract_kr: 본 논문은 근대 한국 불교의 대표적 개혁 인물인 석전 박한영(石顚 朴漢永, 1870-1948)의 교육 철학과 교수법을 탐구하고, 그가 근대적 위기 속에서 추진한 불교 인재 양성 전략과 그 성과를 분석하였다. 박한영은 불교 본래 정신의 회복을 통한 근본적 쇄신, 사회적 변화에 적극 대응하는 참여적 불교 교육, 참다운 인간 형성을 위한 전인적 교육을 중심으로 통합적이고 실천적인 교육관을 제시하였다. 그의 교육 방법은 전통 교학의 내실화, 계율 중심의 교육 실천, 근대적 교수법 및 학문의 적극적 수용을 특징으로 하며, 이는 출가자와 재가자 모두를 포괄하는 포용적 교육으로 발전하였다. 또한, 중앙불교전문학교 등을 중심으로 교육된 제자들은 한국 불교의 현대화와 사회적 확장에 크게 기여하였으며, 그의 교육적 비전은 현대 진보주의 교육, 인간중심 교육, 전통과 현대의 통합 교육, 전체론적 교육 등의 측면에서 현대 불교 교육의 지속 가능한 발전을 위한 이론적 기반을 제공한다.

title_kr: 조사선과 간화선의 사제관계를 바탕으로 한 화두⋅선문답 수행 시스템 설계 연구
title_en: A Study on the Design of the Hwadu and Seon Dialogue (禪問答) Practice System Based on the Master-Disciple Relationship in Josa Seon and Ganhwa Seon
abstract_kr: This study aims to organically integrate the core principles of Josa Seon (祖師禪) and Ganhwa Seon (看話禪), the representative meditative traditions of Korean Seon Buddhism, and to reconstruct them as a five-stage practice system suited to contemporary conditions and technological environments. Josa Seon emphasizes intuitive awakening and embodied mindfulness in daily life, while Ganhwa Seon focuses on the deepening of existential doubt through hwadu (critical phrase) and the deconstruction of ego-identity via Seonmundap (traditional Seon question–answer exchanges; Seon Dialogue, 禪問答). Both traditions pursue intuitive insight prior to language and logic, placing the master–disciple relationship at the center of the practice process.This study interprets the inner structure of these traditions through the integrated sequence of “hwadu–doubt–dialogue–awakening,” and reconstructs the flow of psychological and emotional transformation into five stages: (1) Emotional Grounding – preparing the mind-body condition through emotional stabilization and rhythm regulation; (2) Meta-Cognitive Reflection – observing emotions and thoughts to dissolve ego-identification; (3) Intensive Doubt Practice – deepening immersion through repeated questioning; (4) Cognitive Disruption – inducing perceptual shift through the subversion of language; and (5) Daily Embodiment – sustaining awareness in everyday contexts.The system is designed to unfold non-linearly according to the practitioner’s internal state and can be adjusted in real time through integration with GPT-based language models, emotion analysis, immersion tracking, and feedback reports. It functions as a verbal support tool for teachers within traditional Seon pedagogy, and as a “Digital Seon do-ban (善道伴)”—a virtual companion to support practitioners in the absence of a physical teacher.Furthermore, the proposed system is applicable not only in digital settings but also within traditional Seonbang (Seon practice halls, 禪房) as a structural framework for diagnostic guidance. Ultimately, this study holds both theoretical and practical significance by presenting a model of applied Seon Buddhism that integrates traditional meditative principles with contemporary technologies to promote sustained self-awareness and contemplative immersion.

title_kr: 현대 한국사회의 죽어감과 사유(死有) 명상
title_en: Dying and Meditation in Modern Korean Society
abstract_kr: The number of elderly welfare facilities nationwide was 387,391 in 2023. It can increase to 703,970 by 2040. Almost all members of modern Korean society are excluded from their homes and society, and are bound to die alone in hospitals and facilities. Even if the world calmly dies in solitude, humans are dignified beings with Buddha's nature and must die with dignity.Those who are dying after reaching medical limits in welfare facilities for the elderly should be provided with an opportunity to gain insight into the finiteness of life, impermanence, and inevitability of death, to bravely lead their own dying, and to choose the best way to transform themselves into mature and integrated human beings using the upcoming moment of death as coordinates.In the future, anyone can do it without restriction even when he or she lies alone in a hospital or welfare facility for the elderly, suffering from illness, gasping for breath, and dying, and returning to his or her original position of intimacy in the name of pre-trained Buddhist meditation and deadness.

title_kr: 생명존중 교육을 위한 명상상담 지도자의 역할과 과제
title_en: The Role and Tasks of Leaders in Meditation and Counseling for Life Respect Education
abstract_kr: There are studies that the relationship between the instructor and the learner plays an important role in the effectiveness of education in psychological education. In suicide prevention counseling, there is also research that the counselor's supportive relationship with the client has a decisive influence on the effectiveness of counseling. Therefore, the purpose of this paper is to focus on the importance of the leader's personality, examine the psychology and role of counseling instructors who are influenced by social values and have psychological tasks, and discuss the necessity of self-care and meditation for instructors.We examined that counselors also live under the influence of authoritarian and discriminatory values ​​in our society, and that this can affect respect for clients. In addition, self-healing to overcome the counselor's personal psychological tasks is important. For counselors who care for others, 'meaning burnout' can especially affect them because they cannot find meaning in what they do. In order to prevent and overcome burnout, counselors need to have an integrated perspective on the purpose of their lives and the meaning of their work, and they need to continuously take care of themselves. Counselors should pursue holistic growth and cultivate their expertise, and self-awareness through meditation can help in this process.

title_kr: 전통선 응용 현대 선명상 프로그램 개발 및 효과- 성인의 마음 챙김과 사회심리적 건강을 중심으로 -
title_en: Development and Effectiveness of a Modern Seon Meditation  Program Using Traditional Seon: Focusing on Adult Mindfulness and  Social Psychosocial Health
abstract_kr: The purpose of this study is to develop a modern Seon Meditation program that combines modern science and meditation based on the traditional Seon Meditation program centered on the existing Josaseon and Ganhwaseon, and to verify its effectiveness. This program introduced modern scientific theories such as quantum entanglement and quantum potential to the core concepts of traditional Seon Meditation, and also included psychological elements such as self-esteem, gratitude, and the practice of compassion. In addition, the effectiveness of the program was maximized by utilizing Byron Katie's four question techniques and the new-six paramitas.To conduct the study, 52 participants were recruited and divided into experimental and control groups. The experimental group participated in the Seon Meditation program that combined theory and practice for 120 minutes once a week for a total of 10 sessions from June 2024, and the researcher measured mindfulness and social psychological health scales before and after the start of the program. The participants wrote a daily practice log and submitted an interim and final impressions, and the researcher analyzed the contents based on the contents. The data were statistically processed using the SPSS 25.0 program, and the performance logs and reflections were analyzed for content to derive research results.As a result of the study, first, the experimental group showed a significant effect in mindfulness ability, especially in attention and concentration. Second, the experimental group's overall social and psychological health improved. Third, as the session progressed, the experimental group's sitting time increased and concentration improved, and their daily awareness and positive thinking continued to improve. In addition, a participant whose physical health had deteriorated recovered her faith and self-confidence through the Seon meditation. This study proved that a program that combines modern elements with traditional Seon meditation has a positive effect on promoting mindfulness and social and psychological health in adults.
